content.text:
Confirmed: the ordering (`createDualView()` before `myPopupActions = createPopupActions()`) had existed unchanged for a long time and was harmless, because `createDualView()` previously registered mouse listeners that referenced `myPopupActions` lazily (read at click time, long after the constructor finished). It only became a bug when `b7705a4e7a36eacf58c16c5d2a4a4a36fbe97920` replaced that lazy-lookup pattern with `PopupHandler.installPopupHandler(..., myPopupActions, ...)`, which captures the `myPopupActions` value eagerly at call time via a `@NotNull final ActionGroup group` parameter — at that point in the constructor, `myPopupActions` was still `null` (not yet assigned), permanently baking in a `null`/invalid action group for the popup menus.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b7705a4e7a36eacf58c16c5d2a4a4a36fbe97920

## Reasoning
(1) I diffed the fix commit `09fa087` and saw it only reorders two statements in the constructor of `FileHistoryPanelImpl`: moving `myPopupActions = createPopupActions();` to run *before* `createDualView();` instead of after. I then searched `createDualView()`'s body and found it calls `PopupHandler.installPopupHandler(myDualView.getTreeView(), myPopupActions, ...)`, i.e. it consumes `myPopupActions` directly. I walked the full history of this file with `git log -p --follow` and `git log -S"installPopupHandler"` to see when that dependency was introduced.

(2) Commit `b7705a4e7a36eacf58c16c5d2a4a4a36fbe97920` ("Thu Feb 11 2016") refactored `createDualView()` from manually-added anonymous `PopupHandler` mouse listeners (whose `invokePopup()` method read the `myPopupActions` field lazily, at the moment the user actually right-clicked — long after the constructor had finished and the field was set) to calling the utility `PopupHandler.installPopupHandler(component, @NotNull final ActionGroup group, ...)`. That static method captures the passed `group` argument into a `final` local variable used inside its own internal anonymous `PopupHandler`, i.e. the value of `myPopupActions` is captured **at call time**, not read lazily later. Since the surrounding constructor still called `createDualView()` before assigning `myPopupActions = createPopupActions()`, this commit silently changed the method from "safe because it resolves the field after full construction" to "broken because it bakes in whatever the field held at call time" — which was `null` (its default/blank-final value), permanently installing a `null` action group for the file-history popup menu (violating the `@NotNull` contract on `installPopupHandler`).

(3) Evidence: `git show b7705a4e7a36eacf58c16c5d2a4a4a36fbe97920 -- .../FileHistoryPanelImpl.java` shows this exact refactor is the *entire* change in that commit for this file, and the surrounding constructor order (`createDualView()` then `myPopupActions = createPopupActions()`) was unchanged going back further in history (verified via the parent revision) — confirming the ordering itself wasn't the original defect; it only became dangerous once `installPopupHandler`'s eager/`@NotNull` capture semantics were introduced by this commit. The fix commit's only change — reordering the two statements so the field is assigned before `createDualView()` runs — directly neutralizes the defect this commit introduced, with no other intervening commits touching either the ordering or the `installPopupHandler` call.

I'm fairly confident in this identification since the causal chain (lazy field read → eager parameter capture) is clear and the fix is a minimal, surgical reversion of the exact dependency this commit created. The main residual uncertainty is whether this was actually ever manifested as a reported NPE/bug in practice versus simply "popup shows no actions silently" — but either way, this commit is the root cause of the ordering-sensitivity that the fix addresses.
